display.purpose: Hero headlines only. One per page at 800 weight.

headline.purpose: Section titles (h2). Anchors sections without competing with the hero.

body.purpose: Default prose. Capped at 65–75ch line length.

label.purpose: Button text, navigation links, footer. Semibold for presence at small sizes.

mono.purpose: Code snippets and technical labels. Present but not prominent.

narrative.overview: A clean, well-lit workspace. Tools within reach, nothing on the surface that isn't used. The design recedes so the words can speak. Inkwell sits within the AT Protocol publishing ecosystem alongside Standard.site (technical manifesto), Leaflet (approachable sophistication), and Pckt (utilitarian minimalism). It bridges these worlds — the native iOS client that feels like it belongs. The personality is calm, trustworthy, and editorial. The system draws from iA Writer's minimalism, Linear's blog clarity, and the AT Protocol ecosystem's indie-web confidence: technical without being cold, warm without being beige, polished without being corporate. Warmth comes from typographic authority and accent placement, not from tinted backgrounds.
keyCharacteristics: Typography-first hierarchy: weight, size, and spacing do the work; color is secondary
Cool-toned base: the palette leans into a crisp, cool off-white — warmth comes from typography and accent, not tinted backgrounds
Flat elevation: surfaces are differentiated by tonal value alone — no box-shadows
Single-accent discipline: one green accent used sparingly; its rarity is the point
Light/dark parity: every color decision works in both schemes via light-dark()
Restrained interaction: hover states are subtle tonal shifts, not bounces or pulses
Ecosystem-native: the design feels at home next to Standard.site, Leaflet, and Pckt — indie polish, not corporate sheen

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Accent Green is used on ≤10% of any given screen. A primary button, a link, or an icon — pick one focal point per section. If everything is accented, nothing is.

rules.name: The Cool Canvas Rule
rules.body: The Paper background is cool-tinted (hue 260), not warm. Warmth in this brand is carried by typographic authority and accent placement, not by beige backgrounds. A warm off-white body bg is the single most common AI-generation tell; this rule exists to prevent it.

rules.name: The Tonal Surface Rule
rules.body: Cards and containers are distinguished from the background by tonal value alone (a 0.01 L difference in OKLCH plus a chroma step), never by borders heavier than 1px or by box-shadows. If you can't tell a card from the page without a shadow, the tonal step is too small.

rules.name: The Typography-First Rule
rules.body: Visual hierarchy is established through weight, size, and spacing — never through color splashes. If a heading needs a color accent to feel important, the weight or size is wrong.

rules.name: The One Display Rule
rules.body: The hero h1 is the only element at Display weight (800) on any page. Section headings step down to Headline (700). Two display-weight elements on the same page compete; one wins.

rules.name: The Flat-at-Rest Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. If shadows are ever introduced (for a modal, dropdown, or tooltip in a future app shell), they appear only as a response to functional need, never as decoration.

rules.name: The No-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Box-shadow is prohibited on cards, containers, and static elements. Tonal differentiation is the only mechanism for distinguishing surfaces from the background.

dos: Do establish hierarchy through typography (weight, size, spacing) before reaching for color
Do use the single accent (Accent Green, #139500) on ≤10% of any given screen
Do differentiate cards from the background through tonal value (Surface vs Paper), never through box-shadows
Do keep the body background cool-toned (hue 260) — the AT Protocol ecosystem is muted and technical, not warm and beige
Do use text-wrap: balance on h1–h3 for even line lengths
Do cap body text lines at 65–75ch
Do test every color against its background for ≥4.5:1 contrast (body) and ≥3:1 (large text)
Do provide a prefers-reduced-motion fallback for every animation
Do support both light and dark color schemes via light-dark()
Do trust the reader — the AT Protocol audience is technically literate; state the value clearly without over-explaining
donts: Don't use gradient text, side-stripe borders, or glassmorphism — these are prohibited
Don't use the SaaS startup template kit: no gradient hero backgrounds, no animated metric counters, no generic tech-company sheen
Don't add tiny uppercase tracked eyebrow labels above section headings
Don't use numbered section markers unless the sections form a genuine ordered sequence
Don't lean into warm-tinted cream/beige as the body background — the Paper token is cool-tinted (hue 260)
Don't use position: absolute inside overflow: hidden containers for dropdowns
Don't animate CSS layout properties — use transform and opacity for compositor-only animations
Don't over-explain the AT Protocol to the audience — link to atproto.com for background; the site sells the app, not the protocol
